subsystems.role: keeps the plant's control layer reachable only through defined, monitored paths.

subsystems.name: Hardened controllers and endpoints
subsystems.role: removes easy ways into programmable logic controllers, HMIs and engineering workstations.
parts: centralised patch management on plant outage windows

subsystems.name: Identity and remote access
subsystems.role: lets operators and vendors work without exposing the plant.

buildSteps.title: Inventory every device and link
buildSteps.detail: Map each controller, sensor, historian, analyser and workstation, including undocumented remote links left by equipment vendors — most breaches start from assets nobody tracked.

buildSteps.title: Draw zones and conduits
buildSteps.detail: Split the site into field, control, supervisory and enterprise zones, and define exactly which data may cross each boundary and in which direction.

buildSteps.title: Harden what you already have
buildSteps.detail: Change default credentials, disable unused services, enforce signed firmware, and schedule patching into planned shutdowns so a security fix never forces an unplanned loss of a batch.

buildSteps.title: Insert monitored choke points
buildSteps.detail: Install firewalls and, where data only needs to flow one way, unidirectional gateways; copy traffic to an intrusion-detection system tuned to the plant's industrial protocols.

buildSteps.title: Layer process-physics checks on top
buildSteps.detail: Compare temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen and feed-rate readings against what the biological model says is possible, so an attacker changing a setpoint is caught even if the network traffic looks legitimate.

buildSteps.title: Secure the AI layer
buildSteps.detail: Record where training data came from, sign and version each model, test it against deliberately corrupted inputs, and require human confirmation for changes to critical setpoints.

buildSteps.title: Lock down the supply chain
buildSteps.detail: Require software and firmware bills of materials from vendors, verify signatures before installation, and restrict vendor access to scheduled windows through a monitored jump host.

buildSteps.title: Rehearse failure
buildSteps.detail: Run tabletop and live exercises, restore from offline backups, and confirm operators can run the plant manually if the control network must be disconnected mid-batch.

prerequisites.tech: Industrial network visibility and segmentation tooling
prerequisites.why: you cannot defend devices and protocols you have never enumerated.
IEC 62443 gives a common zone-and-conduit framework that vendors, operators and auditors can design against.
OPC UA can sign and encrypt traffic, but older protocols such as Modbus were designed with no authentication at all and remain widespread.

prerequisites.tech: Hardware root of trust in controllers
prerequisites.why: secure boot and tamper-resistant key storage exist in newer equipment but not across installed fleets.
practices such as signed models and data lineage are emerging rather than standard in industrial deployments.

pathway.milestone: segmented control networks with intrusion detection at large biomanufacturing and AI data-centre sites
pathway.unlocks: a plant can lose its enterprise network without losing control of the process.

pathway.milestone: AI-assisted anomaly detection trained on process physics deployed plant-wide
pathway.unlocks: detection of subtle setpoint manipulation, not just known malware signatures.

pathway.milestone: hardware-rooted controllers and signed firmware as default, backed by certification schemes buyers and insurers require
pathway.unlocks: supply-chain trust and easier regulatory sign-off.

pathway.milestone: formally verified control policies with automatic safe-state fallback in largely autonomous plants
pathway.unlocks: higher automation without accepting a single point of digital failure.
